html:
SMTO-GML-0041 — Gmail sent back a reply SMTO couldn't read

GUID: b005fa8b-6714-4f25-bea1-2a6dae1b8df3
Slug: gmail-response-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO got an answer that didn't look like it came from Gmail, for example a web page from a network filter or a Wi-Fi sign-in page, and couldn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running SMTO, open gmail.com in a browser. If a Wi-Fi sign-in or 'blocked site' page appears, complete or resolve it first. Pages like these replace Gmail's answer with something SMTO can't understand.
  2. If you use a work network or VPN, ask your network administrator whether a proxy or filter changes traffic to Google. A proxy that rewrites Google's answers causes exactly this error.
  3. If the Task was sending or changing email, check Sent, Drafts or Trash in Gmail first, then ask SMTO once, only for what is still missing. The change may have happened even though SMTO couldn't read the answer, and repeating it won't help until the network is fixed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the Gmail request and shows the results in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO so they can check what answers on the server's connection to Google. Don't keep repeating the same request while the network problem remains.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail or Google OAuth HTTP response body could not be decoded as JSON, so the Gmail client raised GmailApiError without an HTTP status.

What this means

  • Response JSON decoding raises JSONDecodeError after reading the Gmail/OAuth HTTP response body. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Response JSON decoding raises JSONDecodeError after reading the Gmail/OAuth HTTP response body.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe response status/content type and proxy/endpoint selection without publishing tokens or raw bodies.

How to fix it

  • The response was not valid JSON, typically an HTML page from a proxy, captive portal, TLS-intercepting firewall or a provider error page. Request https://gmail.googleapis.com/ from the Server host to see what answers and fix the proxy or network routing. A statusless failure on a write is treated as an unknown effect, so inspect mailbox state before resubmitting any write.
  • Check provider availability and the endpoint/proxy response. For a mutation, inspect provider state before repeating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A complete valid provider response is parsed, with original mutation state reconciled when needed.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
